content: Neither the glory of the emperor nor the sorrow of the beggar will endure.
author: Persian Proverbs
sourceWork: Classical Sufi Lore & Divan of Hafez
explanation: The peacock struts in golden robes, and the dervish sits in tattered rags. Yet when the curtain of mortality falls, both lie beneath the same spade of dry earth. Why inflate yourself with pride, or torment yourself with shame, over roles that are wiped away at dusk?
practicalInsight: Strip away all social pretension today. Treat everyone you meet as fellow travelers on the brief road to the grave.
reflectionPrompt: What temporary status or social standing are you clinging to that the grave will soon dissolve?
